items.name: Point Lobos State Natural Reserve
items.cost: Vehicle day use $10; weekend/holiday dive or snorkel reservation $30 plus processing fee
items.description: State natural reserve of headlands, coves and meadows three miles south of Carmel on Highway 1, with trails, the Whalers Cabin museum and protected kelp-forest waters offshore.
items.notes: No dogs anywhere in the reserve, including in parked cars. Bikes allowed on paved roads only, not trails. Diving only at Whalers and Bluefish coves, with proof of certification and a reservation. Tours, buses and school groups need a permit or reservation.

items.name: Carmel Mission Basilica
items.cost: Adults $15, seniors (62+) $12, youth (7–17) $8, ages 6 and under free
items.hours: Wed–Thu 10 AM–4 PM; Fri–Sat 10 AM–5 PM; Sun 11:30 AM–5 PM; closed Mon–Tue. Grounds close 15 minutes before the store.
items.description: Historic mission and active Catholic parish; admission covers a self-guided visit to the basilica, museums and grounds.
items.notes: Active parish: the basilica can be closed for weddings, services and events, and closes to visitors 30 minutes before services. Service animals only; no food or drink on the grounds or in the buildings. Closed Thanksgiving, Christmas Day, the day after Christmas and New Year's Day.

items.name: Tor House & Hawk Tower
items.hours: Tours by reservation, Saturdays (limited Fridays) on the hour 10 AM–1 PM
items.description: Stone house and tower that poet Robinson Jeffers built by hand on Carmel Point, now a National Historic Landmark shown on hour-long docent tours.
items.notes: Reservation only; tours capped at six people and suited to ages 10 and up. No photos during the tour. Grounds closed Sunday–Friday except tours; no parking lot, park on neighborhood streets.

items.name: Carmel Beach
items.address: Foot of Ocean Avenue, Carmel-by-the-Sea, CA 93921
items.description: The city's white-sand beach at the bottom of Ocean Avenue, reached by a sand ramp there and by stairways down from Scenic Road; dogs may run off leash under voice control.
items.notes: No lifeguards. Wood fires and bonfires banned; UL-listed propane devices only, south of 10th Avenue. Alcohol allowed 7 AM–10 PM for 21+. No smoking. Stairways at 10th and 12th avenues are closed. Restrooms at the Ocean Avenue lot and at Scenic Road & Santa Lucia.

items.name: Scenic Road & the Scenic Pathway
items.description: Bluff-top walking path along Scenic Road above Carmel Beach, linked to the sand by nine stairways.
items.notes: Dogs must be leashed on the pathway; no smoking. Don't cut across the bluffs to the beach. Vehicles over 7.5 ft tall or 20 ft long may not park on Scenic Road.

items.name: Carmel River State Beach
items.description: Mile-long beach on Carmel Bay where the Carmel River forms a lagoon that serves as a bird sanctuary for waterfowl and songbirds.
items.notes: Dogs allowed. Beach fires banned on Monterey District state beaches; a raised, self-contained gas camp stove is allowed for cooking. Parking lot at the end of Carmelo Street.

items.name: Monastery Beach (San Jose Creek Beach)
items.description: Section of Carmel River State Beach popular with scuba divers.
items.notes: State Parks warns that swimming, wading or walking near the water here can be extremely dangerous. Beach fires banned.

items.name: Garrapata State Park
items.description: Northernmost Big Sur state park, 6.7 miles south of Rio Road, with two miles of coastline, Soberanes Point headlands and a canyon trail that climbs into redwoods.
items.notes: Rocky Ridge Trail closed for hazardous conditions; Soberanes Canyon Trail is open as an out-and-back from the gated east-side trailhead. Dogs only on the beach at Gate 19 and the trails to it. Use care parking along Highway 1.

items.name: Mission Trail Nature Preserve
items.description: The city's largest open space, with several miles of trails (the Flanders, Doolittle, Willow, Mesa and Serra trails) through pine forest, oak woodland, wetland and willow creekside; entrances on Hatton Road, Rio Road and Mountain View Avenue.
items.notes: Dogs allowed under voice control. No bicycles and no restrooms. The Flanders Mansion inside the preserve is closed to the public. The Lester Rowntree Native Plant Garden, just over an acre of California natives, is inside the preserve off the Hatton Road entrance.

items.name: Garland Ranch Regional Park
items.address: 700 West Carmel Valley Road, Carmel Valley, CA 93924
items.hours: Sunrise to sunset; visitor center Thu–Mon 9 AM–3 PM (open Monday holidays)
items.description: The regional park district's first park, rising from the Carmel River to oak savanna on the Santa Lucia crest, with a shaded Garzas Creek trail to a redwood side canyon.
items.notes: No permit needed for the main park; entering the Kahn Ranch section via Hitchcock Canyon Road requires an access permit. Mountain biking limited to the Cooper Ranch area. No overnight use.

items.name: Palo Corona Regional Park (Rancho Cañada unit)
items.hours: Sunrise to sunset; Discovery Center Fri–Sun 10 AM–4 PM (open Monday holidays)
items.description: Over 4,000 acres of coastal hills behind Carmel; from the Rancho Cañada entrance a trail climbs to Inspiration Point (2.2 miles, about 750 ft) for views over the Carmel coast.
items.notes: No permit needed via the Rancho Cañada unit; a permit is required to enter from Highway 1 or to park at the South Bank Trail entrance. Floodplain restoration construction runs 2025–2027, with some areas closed and detours (Detour Trail to the South Bank Trail).

items.name: Forest Hill Park
items.address: Camino Del Monte & Junipero Avenue, Carmel-by-the-Sea, CA 93921
items.description: Neighborhood park with a children's playground, restrooms, basketball court, horseshoe pit and picnic tables, plus tennis courts at the north end.
items.notes: An urgency ordinance bans pickleball throughout the park, including on the tennis courts.

items.name: Earthbound Farm Stand
items.hours: Mon–Sat 8 AM–5 PM; Sun 9 AM–5 PM
items.description: Organic farm stand with a café, market and gardens where visitors can pick their own herbs and berries.
items.notes: Closed Thanksgiving, Christmas Day and New Year's Day.

items.name: Devendorf Park
items.address: Ocean Avenue & Junipero Avenue, Carmel-by-the-Sea, CA 93921
items.description: Lawn park at the top of downtown on Ocean Avenue with public restrooms and a water fountain.
items.notes: No dogs allowed in the park.

site_link.label: Holidays in the Park tree lighting

items.name: First Murphy Park
items.description: Grounds of the 1902 First Murphy house, kept by the Carmel Heritage Society, with public restrooms and a viewing deck looking toward Carmel Bay.

items.name: Picadilly Park
items.address: Dolores Street between Ocean & 7th Avenues, Carmel-by-the-Sea, CA 93921
items.description: Mid-block downtown pocket park with a fountain, benches and public restrooms.

items.name: Marjorie Evans Gallery at Sunset Center
items.address: San Carlos Street at 9th Avenue, Carmel-by-the-Sea, CA 93921
items.hours: Mon–Fri 10 AM–4 PM and during public performances
items.description: Free gallery in Sunset Center's north wing showing two-month exhibitions by Central Coast artists.

items.name: Carmel Farmers' Market
items.address: Sixth Avenue between Junipero & Mission Streets, Carmel-by-the-Sea, CA 93921
items.description: Weekly street market with certified organic produce, eggs, plants, cut flowers and prepared foods such as bread, hummus and pizza.
items.notes: Dogs are not allowed in the market area (Health Department rule).

items.name: Downtown Carmel wine tasting rooms
items.description: More than 18 wine tasting rooms within walking distance in the village, pouring Monterey County wines.

items.name: Carmel Valley tasting rooms
items.address: Carmel Valley Road, Carmel Valley, CA 93924
items.description: Tasting rooms for wineries of Carmel Valley and Cachagua, a warmer inland region above the coastal fog known for Bordeaux varieties such as Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot.

items.name: Carmel Plaza
items.address: Ocean Avenue & Mission Street, Carmel-by-the-Sea, CA 93921
items.hours: Mon–Sat 10 AM–6 PM; Sun 11 AM–5 PM (many restaurants open later)
items.description: Three-level open-air shopping courtyard on Ocean Avenue with over 40 shops, restaurants, wine tasting rooms and a small brewery, plus fire pits and gardens.
items.notes: Pet-friendly. Parking garage entrance at Mission Street & 7th Avenue.

items.name: The Barnyard Shopping Village
items.description: Shopping village built in 1976 with more than 50 shops, restaurants and galleries set along brick paths and gardens off Highway 1.
items.notes: Free parking.

items.name: The Crossroads Carmel
items.address: Highway 1 at Rio Road, Carmel, CA 93923
items.description: Shopping center at Highway 1 and Rio Road with restaurants, a fish market, chocolate, coffee and a wine tasting room alongside everyday shops.

items.name: Carmel Art Association
items.description: Artist-run gallery founded in 1927 showing work by its 79 local painters, sculptors, weavers and printmakers.

items.name: Center for Photographic Art
items.address: Sunset Center, San Carlos Street & 9th Avenue, Carmel-by-the-Sea, CA 93921
items.description: Nonprofit photography gallery inside Sunset Center with changing exhibitions.

items.name: Sunset Center
items.address: San Carlos Street at 9th Avenue, Carmel-by-the-Sea, CA 93921
items.hours: Box office Mon–Fri 12–4 PM, and from two hours before each show
items.description: The village's main performing-arts venue, hosting touring music, theater, dance and Carmel Bach Festival concerts, plus free community events.
items.notes: Buy only from Sunset Center's box office or site; $4.50 per-ticket fee online or by phone, waived at the window. Patron parking in the north lot on 8th Avenue.

items.name: Founders Theatre & Circle Theatre (Golden Bough Playhouse)
items.address: Monte Verde Street between 8th & 9th Avenues, Carmel-by-the-Sea, CA 93921
items.description: Pacific Repertory Theatre's renovated home stage in the historic Golden Bough Playhouse, with a small theatre-in-the-round, the Circle Theatre, entered from Casanova Street.

items.name: Outdoor Forest Theater
items.address: Mountain View Avenue & Santa Rita Street, Carmel-by-the-Sea, CA 93921
items.best_time: August–September family musical, then the Carmel Shakespeare Festival in October.
items.description: 540-seat open-air amphitheater from 1910, framed by pines and stage-side fireplaces, in a small city park.
items.notes: Free but limited on-site and street parking in a residential area; don't block driveways. Picnics welcome at shows.

items.name: Monterey Bay Aquarium
items.cost: Adults (18–69) $65, seniors (70+) $50, youth (5–17) $50, ages 4 and under free
items.description: Large public aquarium on Cannery Row devoted to Monterey Bay's ocean life.

items.name: Point Sur State Historic Park (lightstation)
items.cost: Lightstation tour $20 adults, $10 ages 6–17, 5 and under free; Naval Facility tour $10 adults, $5 ages 6–17
items.hours: Guided tours only: lightstation Sat 10 AM & 2 PM, Sun 10 AM, Wed 1 PM; Naval Facility Sat–Sun 10:30 AM
items.best_time: Arrive 30 minutes early; tours are first come, first served.
items.description: Complete turn-of-the-century light station on a 361-foot volcanic rock, about 19 miles south of Rio Road, open only on docent-led walking tours.
items.notes: No reservations, no dogs. The three-hour lightstation tour climbs 360 ft with stairs. Tour times change through the year and tours can be cancelled for weather.

items.name: Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park
items.description: Redwood park along the Big Sur River with the Redwood Grove boardwalk, River Path and Big Sur Lodge.
items.notes: After the Timber Fire, Pfeiffer Falls, Valley View, Oak Grove, Mt. Manuel, Big Sur River Gorge and Pine Ridge trails remain closed. Dogs only on the Warden's Path, River Path, lots and campground.

items.name: Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park (McWay Falls)
items.description: Park 37 miles south of Carmel known for McWay Falls, an 80-foot waterfall onto a beach, plus Partington Cove reached through a rock tunnel.
items.notes: No beach or ocean access at McWay Falls; the beach, Saddle Rock and falls area are closed and trespassers are cited. No dogs.

items.name: Andrew Molera State Park
items.description: Nearly 5,000 acres with 15 miles of trails and the Big Sur river mouth, 20 miles south of Carmel; home to Cooper Cabin, Big Sur's oldest building.
items.notes: Seasonal Creamery Meadow footbridge is removed each winter (installed June 15–Oct 31); Trail Camp closes Nov 1 to about May 1. No dogs.

items.name: Asilomar State Beach
items.description: Sandy beaches, tidepools and a coastal trail below a dune preserve, next to the Julia Morgan–designed Asilomar conference grounds.
items.notes: Dogs on leash allowed on the beach, trails and conference grounds (not in buildings).

items.name: Big Sur coast drive (Highway 1)
items.best_time: Check Caltrans road conditions the morning you go.
items.description: Coastal drive south from Carmel on State Route 1 past Rocky Creek and Point Sur into Big Sur.
items.notes: Caltrans reports 24-hour one-way traffic control between Point Sur and Big Sur through Dec 31, 2026, and between Regents Point and Fernwood for emergency work; expect delays.
